extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: MVBench is a comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark for evaluating the temporal perception capabilities of multi-modal large language models. It covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame, and is built by automatically converting annotations from 11 public video benchmarks into multiple-choice question-answer pairs.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li; Yali Wang; Yinan He; Yizhuo Li; Yi Wang; Yi Liu; Zun Wang; Jilan Xu; Guo Chen; Ping Luo; Limin Wang; Yu Qiao
extraction.citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, and Yu Qiao. MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. arXiv:2311.17005, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MVBench was assembled by selecting videos from 11 public video datasets and automatically converting their open-sourced annotations into multiple-choice question-answer pairs with LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations from 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: MVBench uses an automatic annotation paradigm to generate multiple-choice QAs by converting open-sourced video annotations into this format via LLMs; specifically, ChatGPT is used to generate a question for each video based on the task definition, answer options are constructed either directly from ground-truth annotations or generated by ChatGPT for some tasks, and videos/questions are filtered by criteria such as video diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For all questions, 3 to 5 answer options are randomly sampled from available candidates and shuffled; an LLM is further used to ensure answer options are of similar and reasonable lengths.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current image and video MLLMs are underperforming in temporal understanding; MVBench relies predominantly on temporal understanding instead of spatial understanding capacity; there is a minimal source gap between the instruction data and MVBench, so the evaluation is not strictly out-domain for some tasks; none of the models achieve satisfactory results on position-related tasks; current MLLMs have difficulty generalizing to localization and counting tasks in the absence of related tuning data; VideoChat2 encounters difficulties with complex egocentric navigation and episode reasoning; visual information alone may not be sufficient, and the inclusion of other modalities, such as depth and audio, could prove beneficial
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: All the models and data are publicly available, in order to pave the path to general video understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluating the temporal perception capabilities of MLLMs in the open world; evaluating the comprehension capabilities of MLLMs on temporal understanding in dynamic videos; providing a benchmark for assessing temporal understanding capabilities of MLLMs
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To guarantee that each task is temporal sensitive, we eliminate short clips which generally contain negligible motions, and also delete extremely long videos which often present overly complicated contexts that are hard for evaluation. Hence, we select videos with intermediate duration, primarily ranging from 5s to 35s. To balance the question difficulty, we design the selection criteria for STAR and CLEVRER. For STAR, we enhance the challenge by randomly shifting the start or end points of the video clips, increasing the complexity of localizing specific events. For CLEVRER, we exclude questions that necessitate more than 10 conditions for describing specific events, thus decreasing QA difficulty. For all questions, we randomly sample 3 to 5 answer options from the available candidates, and shuffle the option order.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Motivated by M3IT, we reorganize all data samples in a uniform format, as shown on the bottom right of Fig. 3. There are two keys involved: {'image' or 'video'}, and {'QA'}. The first key indicates the path to the vision data. The second key represents a list that contains task instruction ('i') and question-answer ('q'-'a').
